$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under src/ imports this file.
purpose: The guard ledger for @platos/adapter-postgres-tenancy. One entry per
transaction boundary, tenant-isolation key, compare-and-set precondition,
count filter, unreadable-column refusal and configuration check in the
package, each carrying the file it lives in, the EXACT text that implements
it (`from`), the edit that removes it (`to`), and the NAMED cases that were
seen to go red (`kills`).
A guard nothing can turn red is a guard that is not there. All 22 entries
below were exercised on a real PostgreSQL container before this adapter was
proposed and all 22 were falsifiable, each with at least one named case.
This lives here rather than in README.md because that file is emitted by
scripts/arch/gen-v1-skeleton.mjs and byte-compared by `node
scripts/arch/gen-v1-skeleton.mjs --check`: adoption releases a project's
PLACEHOLDERS, never its scaffolding, so an adopted adapter still owes the
generator its README verbatim.
WIN-258 T7 adds M23-M26 and lifts the count from 22 to 26. M23 is the
sharpest entry in this file, because the mutation IS the code as it stood
at 8f078963: it puts the server timeouts back on the datasource URL as
query parameters. Three of its four kills are in
`pooling.integration.test.ts` and NONE of them could have been in
`client.test.ts`, because the URL the mutant writes is exactly as
convincing as the URL the fix writes and only a real server can tell them
apart -- it answers `current_setting('statement_timeout')` with '0' and
runs a `pg_sleep` to the end.
M25 IS DECLARED WEAK AND NAMED SO. Dropping the `ms` suffix leaves a
mutant that is still correct against PostgreSQL today, because all three
settings default to milliseconds; what goes red is the spelling
`current_setting` echoes back. It is counted as a kill of the SPELLING and
the entry says so, rather than being counted as a behavioural guard it is
not.
procedure: PROVE THE SUITES GREEN FIRST. The first run of this sweep reported 22 kills
and every one of them was VACUOUS: `packages/contexts/tenancy/dist` had been
cleaned by an earlier `tsc -b --clean`, so every suite failed to load its
import and would have 'died' against any mutation at all, including none.
The driver now runs each suite set unmutated and refuses to sweep unless it
is green, and treats a module-load failure as VACUOUS rather than as a kill.
A mutation sweep that never saw green is a sweep that measured nothing.
For one entry: build @platos/tenancy-database and @platos/context-tenancy,
replace its `from` with its `to` in the named file, run
`pnpm exec vitest run <suites>` from the package (with DOCKER_HOST set for
the integration suites), and confirm a NAMED case goes red. Then revert and
confirm green.
FIFTEEN OF THE TWENTY-TWO NEED A REAL POSTGRESQL. They are the entries
whose suites end in `.integration.test.ts` -- M01-M14 and M22 -- and none
of them could have been written against a double: M01-M06 are about a
transaction that has to exist, M07-M09 about a compound index that has to
be the thing doing the filtering, M10 about an UPDATE ... WHERE that has
to affect zero rows on the second call, and M22 about statements a client
has to actually send.
TWO ENTRIES ARE ABOUT THE DOUBLE, NOT THE ADAPTER, and they are the reason
the conformance scenario exists. M10's kill is the conformance case rather
than a dedicated one, because both stores are asked the same question and
the fake answers it correctly; the pin is `firstConsume: 1, secondConsume: 0`
by exact value. And the suite's FIRST run failed on
`OperatorSession_tokenHash_check` -- a CHECK constraint in the migrations
that neither schema.prisma nor the fake carries -- which is a defect this
ledger did not have to look for.

mutations.note: Declared as a WEAK guard rather than a strong one, and named so it cannot be mistaken for a strong one. All three settings happen to default to milliseconds, so the mutant is still CORRECT against PostgreSQL today; what goes red is the value `current_setting` echoes back ('400' rather than '400ms'). The guard is against a future setting whose unit is not ms, and the kill is real but is a kill of the SPELLING, not of the behaviour.
